variables.title: Variables (Hold/Pattern Space)
variables.notes: Sed doesn't have named variables. It uses a 'pattern space' (current line) and a 'hold space' (buffer). h=copy to hold, G=append hold to pattern.

data_types.title: Data Types (Text Streams)
data_types.notes: Sed only processes text streams. Numbers and strings are manipulated using regular expressions.

operators.title: Operators (Commands)
operators.notes: Commands act as operators: s/ (substitute), d (delete), p (print). Semicolons chain commands.

conditionals.title: Conditionals (Addresses/Patterns)
conditionals.notes: Addresses (regex or line numbers) before a block { } act as conditionals (if matches, then execute).

for_loop.title: For Loop (Global Substitution)
for_loop.notes: The 'g' flag in substitution acts like a loop, replacing all occurrences on a line instead of just the first.

while_loop.title: While Loop (Branching/Labels)
while_loop.notes: Loops are created using labels (:a) and branching on success (t a) or unconditional branching (b).

functions.title: Functions (Reusable Scripts)
functions.notes: Sed lacks functions. Logic is encapsulated in script files (-f) or blocks { }.

arrays.title: Arrays (Multi-line Pattern Space)
arrays.notes: No arrays. The N command appends the next line to the pattern space, allowing multi-line (array-like) processing.

maps.title: Maps (Lookup Tables via Regex)
maps.notes: No native maps. Key-value lookup is achieved by explicitly chaining substitutions.

error_handling.title: Error Handling
error_handling.notes: Very limited. Scripts will halt on syntax errors. The 'w' flag safely writes successful matches to a file.

comments.title: Comments & Script Headers
comments.notes: Sed uses # for comments with script headers.

numbers.title: Numbers & Arithmetic
numbers.notes: Sed supports shell integer arithmetic and numeric expressions.

booleans.title: Booleans & Exit Codes
booleans.notes: Sed evaluates boolean status through exit codes (0 = success) and boolean primitives.

type_casting.title: Type Casting & Coercion
type_casting.code:
str_val="42"
# Arithmetic context forces integer coercion
num=$((str_val + 0))
type_casting.notes: Sed handles type conversion explicitly via type accelerators [type] or arithmetic evaluation.

strings.title: Strings & Quoting
strings.code:
single='Literal single quotes'
double="Expanded: ${USER}"
multiline="Line 1
Line 2"
strings.notes: Sed differentiates between single quotes (literal) and double quotes (variable expansion).

string_formatting.title: String Interpolation
string_formatting.notes: Sed provides in-string variable interpolation and printf formatting.

pattern_matching.title: Pattern Matching & Case
pattern_matching.notes: Sed matches patterns with case statements or switch blocks with glob matching.

range.title: Ranges & Sequences
range.code:
# Brace expansion
for i in {1..10..2}; do
    echo "$i"
done
range.notes: Sed constructs ranges with brace expansion {start..end} or range operators ..

iterators.title: Pipes & Iterators
iterators.code:
while IFS= read -r line; do
    echo "$line"
done < "file.txt"
iterators.notes: Sed streams data elements through command pipelines and loop iteration.

oop_classes.title: Classes / Structured Functions
oop_classes.notes: Sed defines reusable components through classes (PowerShell 5+) or modular functions.

lists.title: Arrays & Collections
lists.code:
items=("apple" "banana" "cherry")
items+=("date")
echo "${items[0]}" # apple
echo "${items[@]}" # all elements
lists.notes: Sed manages arrays using array lists @() or whitespace-delimited shell arrays.

tuples.title: Tuples & Records
tuples.notes: Sed emulates tuples through string delimiters, .NET Tuples, or positional variables.

sets.title: Sets & Unique Lists
sets.notes: Sed models unique sets using associative arrays or underlying runtime sets.

modules_import.title: Sourcing & Modules
modules_import.code:
# Source an external script
source ./utils.sh
# or: . ./utils.sh
modules_import.notes: Sed imports external functions using source (. in POSIX) or Import-Module.
